Issued at 309 AM EDT Sat Sep 26 2026

Today-Tonight... Upper level cutoff low paired with a nor'easter off 
the North Carolina coast will slowly move northward through the day. 
At the surface, broad high pressure will build over the Florida 
peninsula. Locally, breezy northerly winds will persist today, with 
speeds around 10 mph across the interior, and 10-15 mph along the 
coast with gusts to around 20 mph possible at times. Drier air will 
filter down across the local area today, with forecast PW values 
dropping to 0.8-1.3" this afternoon. This will result in little to 
no rain and lightning storm chances today, with the greatest 
potential for rain (PoP 20 percent) occurring across the southern 
Treasure Coast. Seasonable temperatures are forecast today, with 
afternoon highs in the low to mid 80s with heat indices in the 80s 
to potentially up to 90s degrees in the Treasure Coast. Overnight 
lows will be in the 60s. 

Despite the pleasant weather, beach conditions are forecast to 
remain poor to hazardous today. Seas will be slow to subside through 
the day. A high risk of rip currents remains in effect today, with 
breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet, resulting in rough hazardous surf 
persisting. Entering the surf is strongly discouraged! 

Sunday-Monday... The upper level cut-off low and associated 
nor'easter off the eastern seaboard Sunday will lift northward, 
eventually pushing onshore across the New England coast by Monday. 
At the surface, broad high pressure will continue to build over the 
Florida peninsula as high pressure across the western Atlantic 
slowly builds westward towards the Caribbean. Locally, drier air 
will filter across the area, with forecast PW values falling to 1.0-
1.2" areawide. This will result in little to no rain and storm 
chances into early next week. The highest rain chances (PoP 20 
percent) will be across the southern Treasure Coast on Monday. The 
pressure gradient slackens over the local area, with winds becoming 
light and variable through the period. Seasonable temperatures are 
forecast into early next week. Afternoon highs are forecast to be in 
the low to mid 80s Sunday, and mid to upper 80s on Monday. Peak heat 
indices will be in the upper 80s to low 90s on Monday. Overnight 
lows will be in the 60s, possibly reaching 70 degrees along the 
coast by Monday. 

Poor to hazardous conditions are forecast to continue at the beaches 
through at least Sunday as seas are slow to subside through early 
next week. A high risk of rip currents is forecast through at least 
Sunday, though it will may continue into Monday as well. Breaking 
waves of 3 to 6 feet will also persist, so rough, hazardous surf 
will also be present. Overall, entering the ocean is strongly 
discouraged through at least Sunday.  

Tuesday-Friday... Upper level trough over the eastern seaboard early 
next week will push off shore by midweek. A surface high pressure in 
the western Atlantic will slowly shift northward through the period. 
Model solutions begin to diverge later into the period. The global 
models vary slightly in timing and location of a mid-upper level 
trough and associated surface low swinging across the CONUS, 
bringing the attendant surface front towards Florida mid to late 
next week. Locally, onshore winds will remain in place, although 
there is some uncertainty if the winds will be more easterly or 
southeasterly. Moisture looks to recover slightly, however exactly 
how much remains in questions as forecast PW values range from near 
to below normal to above normal depending on the model. This has 
resulted in decreasing confidence in forecast rain chances and heat 
impacts. For now, have rain chances broadly increasing from 
near/below normal Tuesday, becoming near/above normal Wednesday 
through Friday (with rain chances increasing each day). Lightning 
storm chances also return on Wednesday onward. Temperatures will be 
seasonably warm once again, with afternoon highs in the mid to upper 
80s. Due to the increase in moisture, peak heat indices will be in 
the mid to upper 90s.
